subject: Activation link broken by Outlook mobile wrapping -> no PO visibility
messages: From: Susan Mills To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700 Subject: Can't see POs after accepting invite (screenshot attached) Hi Marcus, We accepted the supplier portal invite you sent this morning for Calyx Therapeutics, and the account was created, but our user can’t see any Purchase Orders (POs) under the vendor profile. The acceptance flow reported a success page, but POs that were previously visible via the legacy portal aren't showing up. I attached a screenshot of the success page and the Accept email from our end — it looks like Outlook mobile inserted line breaks into the activation link and the token part looks truncated in the preview. Can you check whether that could cause a problem? We tried on desktop and it worked for one user, but three of our team used mobile and they’re missing POs. Screenshot: screenshot-accept-flow.png (PNG, 98KB) Thanks, Susan Mills Senior Procurement Manager Calyx Therapeutics procurement@calyxthera.com -- On Mon, Apr 27, 2026 at 09:05, Calyx Procurement wrote: > Activate your account: https://supplier.redwood.ai/accept?token=eyJhbGciOiJ...longtoken... > > (Email forwarded from mobile client) From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai Cc: Susan Mills Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700 Subject: Fwd: Can't see POs after accepting invite (screenshot attached) Ben / Jordan — forwarding Calyx's report. Key facts from Susan: three users accepted invites from Outlook mobile and now those accounts exist but do not show historical POs tied to the vendor record. One desktop acceptance worked and POs are visible for that user. Repro steps we should try: - Look at the Accept endpoint logs for the session IDs tied to Calyx today (ticket link below). - Check whether the token we issue is being truncated by URL-wrapping (soft line breaks) and whether our acceptance handler treats a truncated token as a different ephemeral identity (creating a shadow account not bound to vendor id). - Confirm whether tenant binding uses email local-part normalization (plus-addressing) or token exact-match. Attached: screenshot-accept-flow.png (from customer). Customer-facing ask: Can we either map those shadow accounts to the existing vendor id or reissue invites in a format that avoids mobile wrapping? TIA — Marcus Product Manager, Onboarding Redwood Inference From: ben_carter@redwood.ai To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 14:33:00 -0700 Subject: Re: Fwd: Can't see POs after accepting invite (screenshot attached) Thanks for the ping — I dug into the logs and pulled the accept events for calyxthera.com from 09:00–12:00 PDT. Quick findings: - We see three Accept requests that return 200 with body {status: "accepted"} but the acceptanceEvent contains accept_token values that differ by small suffixes (one looks truncated: ends with "...Q2f\n" — that newline looks like a client-wrapped token). - Our downstream tenant-join worker uses accept_token -> vendor_id mapping in the canonical index; if token is truncated it creates a new ephemeral identity and emits a vendor_link event that binds to a different internal subject_id (shadow). - The desktop acceptance used a full token and joined the existing vendor_id as expected. Actionable items: 1) We can map the shadow subject_ids for the three mobile users to the canonical vendor_id retroactively. That requires a db-fix with a small migration script (I can run after review). 2) We should mitigate future mobile-wrapping by: - Reissuing invites with a shortened token key (short-lived GUID) OR - Sending a plain-text activation code users paste into the portal as fallback, and updating the invite email to include the last 6 chars of the token so customers can confirm no truncation. I recommend we do (1) now to restore access, then implement (2a) and (2b) as follow-ups. Logs: https://internal-logs.redwood.ai/ingest/sessions?query=calyxthera.com%20accept HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/HT-98721 Ben Senior SRE, Redwood Inference From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 08:42:00 -0700 Subject: Re: Fwd: Can't see POs after accepting invite (screenshot attached) Quick technical readout from the token parsing side: - The accept token is a base64url-encoded JWT with a ~300 char payload. Many mobile clients (Outlook iOS/Android) insert soft line breaks at ~76 characters in plaintext views which can result in the link query param being split when the client follows the link or when the link is rewritten by a mail gateway. The trailing "\\n" we saw in the logs indicates the client probably sent the URL with an embedded newline. - Our accept handler currently URL-decodes and then does an exact token lookup in accept_tokens table. We have a tolerant parse that strips whitespace, but it only strips leading/trailing spaces, not embedded newlines inside the token string. Proposed short-term fixes (to deploy today): - Update accept handler to normalize token by removing all whitespace and any common soft-break characters before lookup (fast patch). - Run a one-off reconcile job to merge subject_ids where accept events within the same vendor email domain share other identifiers (email, org_vat, or original invite_id). I will prepare a safe upsert script (will include backup and dry-run). Longer term: - Consider issuing numeric activation codes (6–8 digits) as a mobile-friendly fallback with paste-in flow. - Update email template: wrap token section in ... and provide an explicit "If link looks broken, copy this code" fallback. I can land the normalization patch and staging migration today; Ben, can you coordinate DB migration window? Jordan Engineering Manager, Onboarding Runtime From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai To: Susan Mills Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:10:00 -0700 Subject: Re: Can't see POs after accepting invite (screenshot attached) Hi Susan — thanks for the screenshot and the clear repro. Short update: our engineers found that Outlook mobile was inserting line breaks into the activation token which caused the portal to create "shadow" accounts for the mobile acceptances. We can restore PO visibility for the affected users and we have two parallel fixes: 1) Immediate restore: we will run a reconcile to map the three affected mobile accounts to your canonical vendor record. This will restore their PO visibility. I will schedule the fix for today at 16:00 PDT and will confirm when complete. 2) Prevent recurrence: we will deploy a small server-side patch to strip embedded newlines from accept tokens (deploying today) and also update the invite template with a fallback activation code option and instructions for mobile clients. Would you prefer we proceed with the immediate restore now (16:00 PDT) or schedule for tomorrow morning? If proceed now, please confirm we can perform the fix and that the three affected users are fine with a brief account update (no downtime; they may have to refresh their sessions). Thanks again for the detailed note — apologies for the friction. — Marcus Product Manager, Onboarding Redwood Inference marcus_lin@redwood.ai Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182
